findings.title: UTF-16/32 storage records bypass compact classification
findings.detail: The envelope classifier returns None unless contiguous ASCII marker/storage keys or an ASCII Unicode escape occur in the byte sequence. Valid UTF-16/32 JSON encodes those characters with intervening zero bytes and returns None before json.loads can recognize the storage fields. read then returns those bytes as plain evidence, evidence_exists accepts the regular blob, and audit treats the JSON as a plain record unless raw_utf8 occurs. A compact record can therefore satisfy availability and budget without its payload or tested/command/exit/integrity guards. This source inspection independently confirms the mechanism reported by the concurrent SECURITY reproduction.
findings.requested_change: Classify or reject reserved compact JSON content across JSON-supported encodings before permitting plain fallback. Preserve opaque historical evidence and add UTF-16/32 missing/tampered-payload, metadata-binding and budget regressions.
